chapters.title: The Owl's Riddle
chapters.focus: past continuous · present perfect · first conditional · should

pages.text: It was getting dark when {hero} and {pet} reached the Whispering Forest. The trees were so tall that they hid the moon, and the leaves seemed to whisper their names. {pet} stayed close to {hero}, which was [[unusual|not normal or not common]], because {pet} is normally very brave.

q.q: How was {pet} behaving differently from usual?
options: running ahead to explore the path
q.explain: {pet} “stayed close… which was unusual, because {pet} is normally very brave” — so {pet} was a little scared.

pages.text: After a while they came to a fork in the path. An old sign said “Left: the River. Right: the Hollow Oak.” While they were deciding, a firefly landed on {hero}'s hand. “I've lived here all my life,” it buzzed. “If you go left, you'll get lost in the [[mist|a thin cloud near the ground that is hard to see through]].”

q.q: Why did the firefly warn them about the left path?
options: They would lose their way in the mist.
The river there was much too deep to cross.
The Hollow Oak was on that side.
Its family lived on that path.
q.explain: “If you go left, you'll get lost in the mist.” (first conditional: if + present, will + verb)

pages.text: They took the right path and soon found the Hollow Oak. Inside, a white owl was [[guarding|watching something to keep it safe]] a glowing page. “I have kept this safe for a hundred nights,” she said, “but I can only give it to someone who answers my riddle: what gets bigger the more you take away?”

q.q: Why hasn't the owl given the page to anyone yet?
options: She wants to keep the page forever.
q.explain: She can only give it to “someone who answers my riddle” — so nobody has answered it yet.

pages.text: {hero} thought for a moment and then smiled. “A hole!” The owl's eyes sparkled. “Correct. You should keep going — I think the next page is somewhere near the lake.” As they walked out of the forest, {hero} noticed that the trees had stopped whispering. Perhaps they were [[relieved|happy because something worrying has ended]] too.

q.q: Where does the owl think the next page is?
q.explain: “I think the next page is somewhere near the lake.”

final.q: Which word from the story means “watching something to keep it safe”?
final.explain: The owl was guarding the page: keeping it safe.

chapters.title: The Lantern Festival
chapters.focus: past continuous · past perfect · present perfect · first conditional · should

pages.text: Every summer, the creatures of the Whispering Forest hold a Lantern Festival, and this year the owl had invited {hero} and {pet} as special guests. When they arrived, the fireflies were hanging paper lanterns on every branch. But one firefly, Pip, was sitting alone on a mushroom, looking [[miserable|very unhappy]].

q.q: Why were {hero} and {pet} at the festival?
options: They were lost in the forest.
Pip had asked them to come.
q.explain: “This year the owl had invited {hero} and {pet} as special guests.”

They weren't lost this time. They came because “the owl had invited” them.
Pip was sitting alone and unhappy. The invitation came from the owl.
Nobody sells anything here. They were “special guests”.

pages.text: “I've ruined everything,” Pip sighed. “I was carrying the biggest lantern when I flew into a branch. Now it has a [[tear|a hole where something has been pulled apart]] in it, and the festival starts at sunset.” {hero} looked at the sky. The sun was already low behind the trees.

q.q: What was Pip doing when the accident happened?
q.explain: “I was carrying the biggest lantern when I flew into a branch.” Was + -ing = the longer action that was going on.

notes.hanging lanterns on a branch: The other fireflies were hanging lanterns. Pip says “I was carrying the biggest lantern.”
notes.sitting alone on a mushroom: Pip sat on the mushroom later, after the accident.
notes.watching the sun go down: It was {hero} who looked at the low sun, after Pip's story.

pages.text: “Don't worry,” said {hero}. “If we work quickly, we'll fix it before sunset.” {pet} found a long pink ribbon in {hero}'s bag, and together they tied it [[carefully|slowly, taking care not to make a mistake]] around the tear. It wasn't perfect, but the paper held. “You should hang it on the oak,” said the owl. “Everyone will see it there.”

q.q: How did they mend the lantern?
options: They tied a ribbon around the tear.
They glued new paper over the hole.
They swapped it for a smaller lantern.
They asked the owl to fly it home.
q.explain: “Together they tied it carefully around the tear.”

There's no glue in the story. {pet} found a ribbon, and “they tied it carefully around the tear.”
They kept the same big lantern and mended it.
The owl only said where to hang it: “You should hang it on the oak.”

pages.text: At sunset, the fireflies flew inside the lanterns and the whole forest began to glow. Pip's lantern, with its pink bow, shone brighter than any of the others. “I've never been so proud,” Pip whispered. Since that night, every lantern in the forest has worn a pink ribbon, in honour of the [[mended|repaired, made whole again]] one.

q.q: Why does every lantern now have a pink ribbon?
options: to remember the night Pip's lantern was saved
because pink ribbons make lanterns brighter
because the owl ordered the fireflies to use them
to stop lanterns from tearing on branches
q.explain: They wear ribbons “in honour of the mended one”: to remember Pip's lantern.

notes.because pink ribbons make lanterns brigh: Pip's lantern shone brightly, but the ribbons are there “in honour of the mended one”, not to add light.
notes.because the owl ordered the fireflies to: The story doesn't say the owl ordered anything. The ribbons are “in honour of the mended one”.
notes.to stop lanterns from tearing on branche: A ribbon can mend a tear, but the story says they wear them “in honour of the mended one”.

final.explain: Pip was miserable: very unhappy about the torn lantern.

notes.very sleepy: Pip wasn't tired. Pip was upset about the torn lantern.
notes.very cross: Pip wasn't angry with anyone, just very sad.
notes.extremely nervous: Nervous = worried about what might happen. Miserable = very unhappy about what has happened.

chapters.title: Firefly Rehearsal
chapters.focus: past continuous · past perfect · present perfect · first conditional · should

pages.text: A week after the Lantern Festival, Pip asked {hero} and {pet} to come back to the Whispering Forest. The fireflies had never practised a sky dance before, and Pip had been chosen to lead it. When {hero} arrived, Pip was [[hovering|staying in the air without flying forward]] above the oak, looking nervous.

q.q: Why had Pip asked them back?
options: to help practise the sky dance
to mend another torn lantern again
to sell pink ribbons to the owl
to find a lost picnic basket
q.explain: Pip invited them because the fireflies needed to practise a sky dance, and Pip was leading it.

notes.to mend another torn lantern again: The lantern was already mended last chapter. This time it's a sky dance.
notes.to sell pink ribbons to the owl: Nobody is selling ribbons. Pip needs help practising the dance.
notes.to find a lost picnic basket: The picnic was in the meadow story. Here Pip needs dance practice.

pages.text: “I've never led a dance before,” Pip admitted. “If we get the [[pattern|a repeated set of steps or shapes]] wrong, the little ones will bump into each other.” While Pip was explaining the steps, two young fireflies were already spinning in the wrong direction. “You should start with a slow circle,” {hero} suggested.

q.q: What was Pip doing when the young fireflies spun the wrong way?
q.explain: “While Pip was explaining the steps, two young fireflies were already spinning…” Was + -ing = the longer action.

notes.hanging lanterns on the oak: Lanterns were last chapter. Now Pip was explaining dance steps.
notes.sitting alone on a mushroom: Pip sat on a mushroom when the lantern tore. Now Pip is leading practice.
notes.mending a pink ribbon: The ribbon already mended the lantern. Pip was explaining the steps.

pages.text: They practised until sunset. {pet} clapped a steady beat with two [[pebbles|small smooth stones]], and the fireflies followed it. If the beat stayed steady, the circles stayed neat. By the time the moon rose, even the youngest firefly had learnt the pattern.

options: by clapping a beat with pebbles
by flying at the front of the whole dance
by telling the owl to leave
q.explain: “{pet} clapped a steady beat with two pebbles, and the fireflies followed it.”

notes.by flying at the front of the whole danc: {pet} stayed on the ground with the beat. Pip led the flying.
notes.by holding the biggest lantern: Lanterns aren't part of this rehearsal. The help was the pebble beat.
notes.by telling the owl to leave: The owl isn't in the way. {pet}'s steady beat helped the circles.

pages.text: “I've never felt so ready,” Pip whispered. Since that night, the fireflies have danced every full moon, and they always start with {pet}'s slow circle. “You should come whenever you can,” Pip told {hero}. “If you visit, we'll save you the best [[spot|a place to sit or stand]] under the oak.”

q.q: Why do the fireflies start with a slow circle now?
options: because the owl ordered a brand-new rule
because fast circles break the lanterns
because Pip forgot all the other steps
q.explain: They “always start with {pet}'s slow circle” — the pattern from rehearsal.

notes.because the owl ordered a brand-new rule: The owl only advised about the lantern before. The slow circle comes from practice.
notes.because fast circles break the lanterns: No lanterns are breaking here. The slow circle is from {pet}'s beat.
notes.because Pip forgot all the other steps: Pip knows the steps. They choose the slow circle because rehearsal taught them.

options: staying in the air in one place
falling straight down to the soft ground
running quickly along a high branch
hiding under a mushroom in the dark
final.explain: Hovering = staying up in the air in one place, like Pip above the oak.

notes.falling straight down to the soft ground: Hovering is staying up, not falling down.
notes.running quickly along a high branch: Fireflies fly; hovering isn't running on a branch.
notes.hiding under a mushroom in the dark: Pip was above the oak, not under a mushroom.

chapters.title: The Full-Moon Sky Dance
chapters.focus: past continuous · past perfect · present perfect · first conditional · should

pages.text: On the night of the full moon, Pip had already gathered every firefly in the Whispering Forest. When {hero} and {pet} arrived, the little ones were practising the slow circle under the oak. Pip was [[glowing|giving off a soft light]] brighter than usual, half proud and half nervous.

q.q: What were the young fireflies doing when {hero} arrived?
q.explain: “When {hero} and {pet} arrived, the little ones were practising the slow circle under the oak.”

notes.mending a torn pink lantern: Lantern mending was an earlier chapter. Tonight they were practising.
notes.queuing for jam tarts: Jam tarts belong to Candy Village. Here they were practising the circle.
notes.sleeping inside the burrow: Nobody is in a burrow. They were practising under the oak.

pages.text: “I've never danced for so many friends,” Pip whispered. “If the beat stays steady, we should be fine.” {pet} had brought the same two pebbles and was ready to clap. While Pip was counting them in, an owl hooted once from a high branch — a friendly [[cue|a signal that tells you when to start]], not a warning.

q.q: What should keep the dance fine, according to Pip?
q.explain: “If the beat stays steady, we should be fine.” First conditional: if + present, will/should.

notes.a louder owl hoot: The owl's hoot is only a cue. Pip trusts the steady beat.
notes.a brand-new lantern: No new lantern is needed for the sky dance.
notes.a race to the meadow: They are dancing, not racing. Pip wants a steady beat.

pages.text: The dance began. Circles of light rose, dipped, and [[braided|twisted together like hair plaits]] through the oak leaves. {pet}'s pebbles kept time, and even the youngest firefly who had struggled at rehearsal now found every step. By midnight the forest had never looked so full of soft gold.

q.q: How did the youngest firefly do tonight?
options: hid the pebbles under a mushroom
q.explain: “Even the youngest firefly who had struggled at rehearsal now found every step.”

notes.stayed home in the burrow: The youngest danced. Nobody stayed in a burrow.
notes.bumped into every circle: Rehearsal bumps were earlier. Tonight the youngest found every step.
notes.hid the pebbles under a mushroom: {pet} kept the pebbles. The youngest found every step.

pages.text: Afterwards Pip hovered beside {hero}. “You've helped us twice now. If you visit next full moon, we'll save you the best spot again.” Since that night, travellers have stopped under the oak just to watch. “You should bring a blanket,” Pip added with a grin. “The show lasts until the [[dew|tiny drops of water on grass in the morning]] arrives.”

q.q: Why might travellers stop under the oak now?
options: to watch the firefly sky dance
to argue about whose kite is higher
q.explain: Travellers “have stopped under the oak just to watch” the dance.

notes.to buy Crumb's jam tarts: Tarts are in Candy Village. Here travellers watch the dance.
notes.to latch a lighthouse shutter: The shutter was at the lighthouse. Here they watch the sky dance.
notes.to argue about whose kite is higher: Kite arguments were at Cloud Castle. Here they watch the dance.

final.q: A “cue” is closest in meaning to…
options: a signal that tells you when to start
a soft blanket for a long dance
a hard pebble used as a drum
a torn lantern that needs mending
final.explain: A cue is a signal to start — like the owl's friendly hoot.

notes.a hard pebble used as a drum: Pebbles kept the beat; the cue was the hoot.
